blocks.html: Upon the knowledge of a person, it is a rich testimony, a great and almost certain proof, that of the face, for having seen and recognised it such long since a; but it is still more assured when one sets down the scars and marks imprinted on the face, or other parts of the body b: as of old, when, in order to recognise the men bound to the service of some public work, it was the custom to imprint signs and marks upon their arms, or to engrave them upon their hands c. For as to the face, so far was it from being the case that anyone dared touch it, that to make ugly and disfigure in any way the face of a man (even were he a slave) by a scar was reputed a thing greatly unworthy, nay cruel and barbarous d, even though it were in punishment of some crime, which the ancients commanded to be [set] upon the face e. For man being, as Lactantius says, the true portrait and image of God f, and his face formed in the image of that divine and celestial beauty g:

notes.citation: Digest 11.7.44 (De religiosis et sumptibus funerum, l. Cum in diversis; Paulus: where a body is buried in several places, the religious place is where the head lies, "of which the image is made, whence we are recognised")
notes.original: l cùm in di uerſis. D. de re ligioſ.

notes.citation: Code 11.10.3 (De fabricensibus, l. Stigmata), book 11 (Arcadius and Honorius: Stigmata, hoc est nota publica, fabricensium brachiis…, to be set on the arms of the arms-factory workers as on recruits, so that those who go into hiding can be recognised)
notes.original: l. ſtigmata-C. de fabricẽ. ſib lib. xj.
notes.gloss: The transcription notes a dash after ſtigmata and a point after fabricẽ though the word runs on.

notes.citation: Code 11.43.10 (De aquaeductu), the penultimate law (Zeno), § 4: the aqueduct-keepers (aquarii, hydrophylaces) to be marked on the hands with the emperor's name; and the said l. Stigmata (C. 11.10.3, note b)
notes.original: l pen. C. de aquæ duct. l. ſtimata. alle.

notes.citation: Digest 7.1.17.1 (De usufructu, l. Locum, § Ex eo) — the P. is the print's sort for §
notes.original: l locum. P. ex eo. D. de vſufruct.
notes.gloss: Evidently on the usufructuary's duty not to abuse or disfigure the slave.

notes.citation: Code 9.47.17 (De poenis, l. Si quis in metallum; Constantine: a man condemned to the games or the mines is not to be branded on the face, since the penalty can be written on his hands or calves, "that the face, which is formed in the likeness of celestial beauty, be not defiled")
notes.original: l. ſi quis in metallnm. C. de pœn.

notes.citation: Lactantius, book 6 as cited — unidentified (sigla incomplete: the note is cut off in the print after "de", presumably de[s Institutions divines], the Divine Institutes); the passage on man as the image and likeness of God is not located in book 6 (cf. Div. Inst. 2.10 and De opificio Dei)
Genesis 1 (1:26–27, man made in the image of God)
notes.gloss: The print's Geneſee is a wrong sort.

blocks.html: And each man is a pattern of God, in a small image (Exemplumque Dei quisque est, in imagine parva) h

notes.citation: Manilius, Astronomica 4.895 (exemplumque dei quisque est in imagine parva); Coras's "book 3" is an error, the line standing in book 4
notes.original: Manile au iij. de l'Aſtio. nomie.
notes.gloss: Exẽplúmq; Dei quiſque eſt, in imagine parua — "and each man is a pattern of God in a small image"; the print's Aſtio nomie is a wrong sort for Aſtronomie.

blocks.html: it would be a kind of sacrilege, and of lese-majesty, to soil, profane and contaminate it by the impression and burning-in of scars. <sup class="mk" data-key="i" data-page="p053">i</sup> And this even were the crime, according to our Canonists, as great and execrable as having, they say, counterfeited the seal of the prince <sup class="mk" data-key="k" data-page="p053">k</sup>.

notes.citation: The said l. Si quis in metallum, Code 9.47.17 (note e)
notes.original: l. ſi quis in metallum. alle gue.

notes.citation: Decretals, X 5.20.3 (De crimine falsi, c. Ad audientiam)
notes.original: c. ad audien tiam. de crim. falſ.
notes.gloss: On the forging of the pope's or prince's letters and seal, treated by the canonists as the gravest of forgeries.
